title: A2 Grammar Quiz 2 — Modal Verbs, Verb Patterns, Prepositions

questions.question: She ___ play the piano very well.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs never add -s in third person. 'She can' (not 'cans').

questions.question: He ___ drive yet — he's only 15.
questions.explanation: Negative of 'can' → 'can't' (or 'cannot'). No double n: never 'cann't'.

questions.question: ___ I use your phone?
questions.explanation: 'May I...?' is a polite way to ask for permission. 'Can I?' is also acceptable in informal contexts.

questions.question: You ___ wear a seatbelt in a car.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong obligation/necessity. It never adds -s or -to.

questions.question: You ___ see a doctor if you feel sick.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice or a recommendation. Softer than 'must'.

questions.question: You ___ smoke in the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Mustn't' = it is forbidden/prohibited. Strong negative obligation.

questions.question: I want ___ learn Spanish.
questions.explanation: 'Want' is followed by to-infinitive: 'want to learn'.

questions.question: She decided ___ stay home.
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by to-infinitive: 'decided to stay'.

questions.question: He enjoys ___ in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' is always followed by -ing form, never by to-infinitive.

questions.question: I don't mind ___ early.
questions.explanation: 'Mind' is always followed by -ing form: 'mind waking'.

questions.question: She likes ___ to music. (preference verb)
questions.explanation: 'Like/love/hate/prefer' can be followed by both to-infinitive and -ing with little difference in meaning (in British English, -ing is more common for habits).

questions.question: She walked ___ the bridge.
questions.explanation: 'Across' = from one side to the other of a flat surface (bridge, road, field).

questions.question: The train went ___ the tunnel.
questions.explanation: 'Through' = movement inside a space from one end to the other (tunnel, forest, door).

questions.question: The cat jumped ___ the wall.
questions.explanation: 'Over' = movement above and to the other side of something (wall, fence, obstacle).

questions.question: I need ___ advice.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable — you cannot say 'an advice' or 'advices'. Use 'some advice'.

questions.question: There isn't ___ bread left.
questions.explanation: 'Any' is used in negative sentences with uncountable nouns: 'isn't any bread'.

questions.question: I have ___ time. Let's talk. (small amount, positive)
questions.explanation: 'A little' = a small (but sufficient) amount, used with uncountable nouns. 'Time' is uncountable.

questions.question: She has ___ friends in this city.
questions.explanation: 'A few' = a small number (positive/sufficient), used with countable plural nouns. 'Friends' is countable.

questions.question: The coffee is ___ hot. I can't drink it.
questions.explanation: 'Too + adjective' means more than desired/needed: 'too hot to drink'.

questions.question: She isn't tall ___ to reach the shelf.
questions.explanation: 'Enough' comes after adjectives: 'tall enough'. Means sufficient amount/degree.

questions.question: He speaks ___ quickly. I can't understand him.
questions.explanation: 'Too + adverb' = more than acceptable: 'speaks too quickly'.

questions.question: What ___ you ___ at 8 pm last night?
questions.explanation: Past Continuous = was/were + -ing. Question with 'you' → 'were you doing'.

questions.question: I ___ a shower when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Past Continuous describes an action in progress when another action interrupted it: 'was having (a shower) when (it rang)'.

questions.question: While she ___, the power cut.
questions.explanation: 'While' + Past Continuous for the background action, Past Simple for the interrupting event.

questions.question: He ___ play football, but he stopped years ago.
questions.explanation: 'Used to + base verb' describes past habits that no longer exist.

questions.question: She ___ like vegetables when she was a child.
questions.explanation: Negative: 'didn't use to + base verb'. After 'didn't', use base form 'use' (not 'used').

questions.question: I was tired. ___, I finished my homework.
questions.explanation: 'However' shows contrast between two ideas: tired, but still finished.

questions.question: I missed the bus ___ I was late.
questions.explanation: 'So' introduces a result: 'missed the bus → so I was late'.

questions.question: She is ___ the situation. (consider)
questions.explanation: 'Consider' ends in a vowel-r pattern, but the stress is not on the last syllable → don't double the r: 'considering'.

questions.question: It ___ rain later. Take an umbrella.
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses possibility (maybe, perhaps). It doesn't add -s or -to.
